## Description

A member of the *P. aurelia* complex (~120 × 40 µm) carrying endosymbiotic *Caedibacter
taeniospiralis* (kappa particles) in its cytoplasm; those that form R bodies (coiled ribbons) are
released into the water and kill the sensitive paramecia that eat them, which vacuolise and die within
hours. Killers are immune.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: not seeded in the default drops (inoculate it from the Catalogue).
<!-- /GENERATED -->

A [released signal](../../mechanics/chemical-signals.md) (R bodies: particles that barely diffuse and persist for
days, spread in biological time); sensitivity belongs to *P. aurelia*. Release rate, diffusion and
half-life are orders of magnitude.

## Not implemented yet

- *Caedibacter* is not a population of bacteria inside the cell; it cannot be lost or gained.
- No mating-type genetics of the *aurelia* complex.
- Helix radius and period are estimates (of the order of Bullington 1925 and Jennings 1906).
- Trichocysts are a defence gene, not discharged organelles that can be counted.
- Contractile vacuole period in fresh water estimated; cytosol osmolarity taken from *P. caudatum*.

## Unique and shared mechanics

The killer side of the [signal toxicity](../../mechanics/chemical-signals.md#signal-toxicity-killer-paramecium)
pair with *P. aurelia*.
